translations.en:
I believe in God, the Father almighty, Creator of heaven and earth,
and in Jesus Christ, his only Son, our Lord,
who was conceived by the Holy Spirit,
born of the Virgin Mary,
suffered under Pontius Pilate,
was crucified, died and was buried;
he descended into hell;
on the third day he rose again from the dead;
he ascended into heaven,
and is seated at the right hand of God the Father almighty;
from there he will come to judge the living and the dead.

I believe in the Holy Spirit,
the holy catholic Church,
the communion of saints,
the forgiveness of sins,
the resurrection of the body,
and life everlasting. Amen.
Meditating on these mysteries during the Rosary conforms our lives to Christ, as each sheds light on human existence from birth to eternal glory.
Joyful Mysteries
These mysteries meditate on the Incarnation and hidden life of Christ, emphasizing Mary's fiat and the early joys of salvation history.
The Annunciation
The Angel Gabriel announces to the Blessed Virgin Mary that she will conceive and bear a son by the power of the Holy Spirit, and that she is to be the Mother of God.
The Visitation
The Blessed Virgin Mary hastens to visit her cousin Saint Elizabeth, the mother of Saint John the Baptist, bringing joy and sanctifying the unborn Baptist with her presence.
The Nativity
Our Lord Jesus Christ is born in a stable in Bethlehem, laid in a manger, as shepherds and angels rejoice at the Savior's humble entry into the world.
The Presentation of the Child Jesus in the Temple

prayers.title: Joyful Mysteries 4: The Presentation of the Child Jesus in the Temple

translations.en: Mary and Joseph present the Child Jesus in the Temple of Jerusalem, offering Him to God the Father according to the Law and fulfilling the prophecy of Simeon.
The Finding of the Child Jesus in the Temple

prayers.title: Joyful Mysteries 5: The Finding of the Child Jesus in the Temple

translations.en: After searching anxiously for three days, Mary and Joseph find the twelve year old Jesus in the Temple, sitting among the doctors, listening and asking questions.
Luminous Mysteries
Mysteries of Light
Added by Pope Saint John Paul II, these focus on Christ's public ministry, revealing Him as the light of the world and inviting deeper contemplation of the Gospel.
The Baptism of the Lord in the Jordan

prayers.title: Luminous Mysteries 1: The Baptism of the Lord in the Jordan

translations.en: Jesus is baptized by John in the Jordan River, where the voice of the Father declares Him the beloved Son, and the Holy Spirit descends like a dove.
The Wedding Feast at Cana

prayers.title: Luminous Mysteries 2: The Wedding Feast at Cana

translations.en: At the wedding in Cana, Christ performs His first miracle at Mary's intercession, changing water into wine and manifesting His divine glory to His disciples.
The Proclamation of the Kingdom

prayers.title: Luminous Mysteries 3: The Proclamation of the Kingdom

translations.en: Jesus preaches the Good News of the Kingdom of God, calling all to repentance, faith, and conversion of heart as He inaugurates His messianic mission.
The Transfiguration
On Mount Tabor, Jesus is transfigured before Peter, James, and John, revealing His divine glory as Moses and Elijah appear, confirming His identity as the Son of God.
The Institution of the Eucharist

prayers.title: Luminous Mysteries 5: The Institution of the Eucharist

translations.en: At the Last Supper, Jesus institutes the Eucharist as the Paschal Banquet, offering His Body and Blood under the appearances of bread and wine for the forgiveness of sins.
Sorrowful Mysteries
These invite contemplation of Christ's Passion, where He embraces suffering out of love, reversing humanity's sin and revealing the depths of divine mercy.
The Agony in the Garden

prayers.title: Sorrowful Mysteries 1: The Agony in the Garden

translations.en: In the Garden of Gethsemane, Our Lord Jesus experiences dreadful anguish, sweating blood in agony as He prays to the Father and submits His will completely.
The Scourging at the Pillar

prayers.title: Sorrowful Mysteries 2: The Scourging at the Pillar

translations.en: Christ is stripped of His garments and cruelly scourged at the pillar by the Roman soldiers, His sacred body torn by lashes for our sins.
The Crowning with Thorns

prayers.title: Sorrowful Mysteries 3: The Crowning with Thorns

translations.en: Jesus is mockingly crowned with thorns by heartless soldiers, who hail Him as a false king, spitting upon and striking the true King of Kings.
The Carrying of the Cross

prayers.title: Sorrowful Mysteries 4: The Carrying of the Cross

translations.en: From the place of condemnation, Jesus carries His heavy Cross through the streets of Jerusalem to Calvary, the site of His Crucifixion, falling under its weight.
The Crucifixion
Our Lord is nailed to the Cross amid the jeers and blasphemies of His enemies, where He endures six hours of agony before commending His spirit to the Father.
Glorious Mysteries
These mysteries celebrate Christ's triumph over death and Mary's share in heavenly glory, filling us with hope for eternal life.
The Resurrection of Our Lord

prayers.title: Glorious Mysteries 1: The Resurrection of Our Lord

translations.en: On the third day, Jesus rises glorious and immortal from the tomb, conquering sin and death, appearing first to Mary Magdalene and the Apostles.
The Ascension of Our Lord

prayers.title: Glorious Mysteries 2: The Ascension of Our Lord

translations.en: Forty days after the Resurrection, Christ ascends body and soul into heaven in the sight of His Apostles, taking His place at the right hand of the Father.
The Coming of the Holy Ghost upon the Apostles

prayers.title: Glorious Mysteries 3: The Coming of the Holy Ghost upon the Apostles

translations.en: At Pentecost, the Holy Spirit descends upon the Apostles gathered with Mary in the Upper Room, empowering the birth of the Church.
The Assumption of the Blessed Virgin

prayers.title: Glorious Mysteries 4: The Assumption of the Blessed Virgin

translations.en: At the end of her earthly life, Mary is assumed body and soul into heavenly glory, free from corruption by reason of her Immaculate Conception.
The Coronation of the Blessed Virgin

prayers.title: Glorious Mysteries 5: The Coronation of the Blessed Virgin

translations.en: In heaven, Mary is crowned Queen of all Angels and Saints by the Most Holy Trinity, reigning in dignity next to her Divine Son, Our Lord Jesus Christ.
O my Jesus, forgive us our sins, save us from the fires of hell; lead all souls to heaven, especially those in most need of thy mercy. Amen.
In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be thy name; thy kingdom come, thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread, and forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us; and lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil. Amen.

Hail Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with thee. Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb, Jesus. Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us sinners, now and at the hour of our death. Amen.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, as it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Hail, Holy Queen, Mother of mercy, hail our life, our sweetness, and our hope. To thee do we cry, poor banished children of Eve; to thee do we send up our sighs, mourning and weeping in this vale of tears. Turn then, most gracious advocate, thine eyes of mercy toward us; and after this our exile, show unto us the blessed fruit of thy womb, Jesus. O clement, O loving, O sweet Virgin Mary. Pray for us, O holy Mother of God, that we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ. Amen.

O God, whose only begotten Son, by His life, death, and resurrection, has purchased for us the rewards of eternal life. Grant, we beseech Thee, that by meditating on these mysteries of the most holy Rosary of the Blessed Virgin Mary, we may imitate what they contain and obtain what they promise, through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.
Saint Joseph, guardian of the Redeemer, protector of the Holy Family—pray for us. Amen.

Remember, O most gracious Virgin Mary,
that never was it known
that anyone who fled to thy protection,
implored thy help,
or sought thy intercession,
was left unaided.

Inspired by this confidence,
I fly unto thee,
O Virgin of virgins, my mother;
to thee do I come,
before thee I stand,
sinful and sorrowful.

O Mother of the Word Incarnate,
despise not my petitions,
but in thy mercy hear and answer me.
Amen.

V. The Angel of the Lord declared unto Mary.
R. And she conceived of the Holy Spirit.

Hail Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with thee. Blessed art thou among women and blessed is the fruit of thy womb, Jesus. Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us sinners, now and at the hour of our death. Amen.

V. Behold the handmaid of the Lord.
R. Be it done unto me according to thy word.

Hail Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with thee. Blessed art thou among women and blessed is the fruit of thy womb, Jesus. Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us sinners, now and at the hour of our death. Amen.

V. And the Word was made flesh.
R. And dwelt among us.

Hail Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with thee. Blessed art thou among women and blessed is the fruit of thy womb, Jesus. Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us sinners, now and at the hour of our death. Amen.

V. Pray for us, O holy Mother of God.
R. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.

Let us pray:
Pour forth, we beseech thee, O Lord, thy grace into our hearts; that we, to whom the Incarnation of Christ, thy Son, was made known by the message of an angel, may by his Passion and Cross be brought to the glory of his Resurrection. Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.

O my God, I am heartily sorry for having offended you, and I detest all my sins because of your just punishments, but most of all because they offend you, my God, who are all good and deserving of all my love. I firmly resolve, with the help of your grace, to sin no more and to avoid the near occasions of sin. Amen.

Eternal rest grant unto them, O Lord,
and let perpetual light shine upon them.

May they rest in peace.
Amen.
